articles.originalTitle: Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year revealed - Dezeen
articles.title: Tree-Top Sauna Named Architecture Project of the Year at Dezeen Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: Located in a Kanagawa forest, the Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna has been named architecture project of the year at the ninth Dezeen Awards, praised for integrating architecture with nature.
articles.content: Nineteen architecture category winners across 11 countries were announced at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony in London. Situated within a forest in Kanagawa, the Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna claimed both the leisure and wellness category win and the overall project of the year award. The master jury commended the minimalist, biophilic project for its spiritual touch. Additionally, Amami House on Amami Ōshima won urban house of the year for sustainable off-grid living, while Jiang Deng Lu in China took the rural house prize. La Querola in Andorra won housing project of the year, Zando Central Market in Kinshasa won the civic category, and the Ismaili Center in Houston secured the cultural project award. The winning designs highlighted sustainable material use, local craft traditions, and community engagement across global contexts.

articles.originalTitle: Has the couple in Jan van Eyck’s ‘Arnolfini Portrait’ been misidentified? - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: New Theory Revives Debate Over Identities in Jan van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait
articles.excerpt: A new theory presented in a National Gallery exhibition catalogue suggests that Jan van Eyck's famous 1434 painting depicts the artist and his wife rather than the merchant Arnolfini family.
articles.content: The identities of the figures in Jan van Eyck's 1434 Arnolfini Portrait, a fixture at London's National Gallery since 1842, are being revisited ahead of an upcoming museum exhibition. Writing in a catalogue essay for Van Eyck: The Portraits, running from 21 November to 11 April 2027, Berlin curator Stephan Kemperdick suggests the male figure is the artist himself and the woman is his wife Margaret. Kemperdick re-examines the prominent Latin inscription and a 16th-century inventory reference to hernoul le fin, arguing it functioned as a later mocking moniker rather than the genuine surname of the Arnolfini family. However, co-curator Nicholas Flory, Emma Capron, and leading scholars Till-Holger Borchert and Maximiliaan Martens express doubt regarding the theory. Critics cite eye-color discrepancies between portraits and maintain that historical inventory references to the merchant family remain solid. The Berlin panel will retain its traditional title for the exhibition, while scholarly debate regarding the room, the woman's supposed pregnancy, and the sitters persists.

articles.originalTitle: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA Receives the First Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture - ArchDaily
articles.title: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA Receives Inaugural Ambasz-MoMA Prize
articles.excerpt: MoMA has selected Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA as the recipient of the first Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture for the Friendship Centre in Bangladesh. The $200,000 award is shared with Fundación Gran Chaco.
articles.content: The Museum of Modern Art has selected Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA to receive the first Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture for the design of the Friendship Centre in Gaibandha, Bangladesh. Described by MoMA as the largest award for a single architecture project, the initiative recognizes architectural practice while supporting environmental action. The $200,000 award is shared between the architectural office and Fundación Gran Chaco, a nonprofit in Formosa, Argentina, which will plant trees in the client's name. According to institute director Evangelos Kotsioris, the awarded project demonstrates how architecture can merge environmental adaptation, historical continuity, and community sensitivity. Completed in 2011, the rural training facility responds to the flood-prone Jamuna River delta by utilizing compacted earthen embankments and local clay bricks. The layout draws inspiration from the ancient city of Mahasthangarh while integrating green roofs and rainwater harvesting pools. The award will be presented at MoMA on December 12, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Best Building Envelope & Cladding Products of 2026 - Architectural Record
articles.title: Highlighting the Best Building Envelope and Cladding Products of 2026

articles.originalTitle: kengo kuma builds a circular thatched house from local timber and earth in japan - Designboom
articles.title: Kengo Kuma Completes Circular Thatched House from Local Timber and Earth in Japan
articles.excerpt: Kengo Kuma and Associates has completed the 137-square-meter Kagaku no Sato Main House in Ibaraki Prefecture, utilizing local timber and compacted earth. The project received an Encouragement Award at the 2026 Wood Design Awards.
articles.content: Kengo Kuma and Associates has completed the Kagaku no Sato Main House in Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan. Serving as the centerpiece for a regional satoyama restoration initiative, the 137-square-meter wooden structure received the Encouragement Award at the 2026 Wood Design Awards. The building features an expansive thatched roof designed with an asymmetric curvature to respond to prevailing winds and sunlight. Twenty-eight timber logs, harvested through regional forest thinning and individually 3D-scanned, form the radial structural shell beneath the thatch. Approximately 5,000 bundles of rice straw, reeds, and grasses were installed by skilled workers to complete the continuous roof surface. Below the deep eaves, a continuous tataki floor made from compacted field earth connects the interior with the surrounding landscape. The walls incorporate local materials including washi paper treated with persimmon tannin to achieve rich brown tones. At the crest of the roof, a traditional grass-covered ridge known as a shibamune allows vegetation to grow and change with the seasons. The completed project successfully integrates historical rural building techniques with contemporary digital fabrication methods.

articles.originalTitle: Wolgang Tillmans wins Henri-Cartier Bresson Lifetime Achievement Award - ArtReview
articles.title: Wolfgang Tillmans Wins Henri-Cartier Bresson Lifetime Achievement Award
articles.excerpt: Photographer Wolfgang Tillmans has won the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Fondation Henri-Cartier Bresson and will receive €35,000 for an exhibition and publication.
articles.content: Photographer Wolfgang Tillmans has won the Henri-Cartier Bresson Lifetime Achievement Award. He will receive €35,000, which will fund an exhibition at the Fondation Henri-Cartier Bresson and a dedicated publication. Following Sophie Calle and Susan Meiselas, Tillmans is the third recipient of the prize recognising photographers who shape the medium. Based between Berlin and London, the photographer gained widespread recognition for his 1990s raw snapshots documenting youth culture and the LGBTQIA+ community. His imagery has appeared across numerous cultural formats, ranging from album covers to paperback book designs. Alongside his artistic practice, which has expanded into camera-less photography, Tillmans has used his platform for political advocacy. His civic engagement includes a 2016 Pro-EU and Anti-Brexit campaign, as well as the establishment of the Between Bridges Foundation in 2017 to support the arts, LGBTQIA+ rights, and anti-racism initiatives.

articles.originalTitle: How Frieze became the latest step in Abu Dhabi's cultural masterplan - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze Abu Dhabi Debuts as the Latest Step in the Emirate's Cultural Strategy
articles.excerpt: Organized in partnership with the Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism, the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi fair aims to elevate regional art globally and position the city as a cultural hub.
articles.content: The inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi art fair opens this month at the Manarat Al Saadiyat cultural hub on Saadiyat Island, taking over from the long-running Abu Dhabi Art fair. Established as a partnership between Frieze and Abu Dhabi's Department of Culture and Tourism, the fair seeks to promote regional artists and better integrate the local market into the global art ecosystem. According to fair director Dyala Nusseibeh, the United Arab Emirates accounted for 45% of all Middle East and North African art buyers in 2025, with growing private collector numbers across the emirate. The fair arrives alongside recent museum openings in the Saadiyat Cultural District, leading up to the scheduled opening of the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi on December 11. Frieze operates under Mari, a live-events business backed by investments from Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund Mubadala and Silver Lake. The event aims to provide greater international exposure for galleries and artists from the Arab world and South Asia, while granting Western galleries access to a new cohort of collectors in the region.

articles.originalTitle: Minimalist, human and crafted – why it’s easy to love Kengo Kuma’s architecture - www.wallpaper.com
articles.title: Kengo Kuma's Architectural Approach Shaped by Traditional Aesthetics and Nature
articles.excerpt: Globally celebrated Japanese architect Kengo Kuma designs minimalist, human-scale spaces that integrate with nature, utilizing natural materials such as wood, stone, and paper across his projects.
articles.content: Globally celebrated Japanese architect Kengo Kuma combines traditional Japanese aesthetics with a modern, crafted approach. Influenced by his childhood in a traditional wooden house and Kenzo Tange's Yoyogi National Gymnasium, Kuma studied at the University of Tokyo and later visited Columbia University. Establishing Kengo Kuma & Associates, the architect focuses on natural materials such as wood, bamboo, paper, and stone. Advocating that structures should dissolve into their settings rather than dominate them, Kuma outlines these principles through concepts like anti-object and makeru kenchiku. His notable projects, including V&A Dundee, Nezu Museum, Japan National Stadium, and the Great Bamboo Wall, feature rhythmic timber joinery, layered eaves, and light-filtering facades. With recent completions including the Capella Kyoto hotel and Kannabiyama Observatory, the prolific studio operates offices in Tokyo, Paris, Shanghai, Beijing, and Seoul.

articles.originalTitle: AI helps conservators uncover lost details in William Merritt Chase painting - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Helps Conservators Uncover Lost Details in Chase Painting
articles.excerpt: A William Merritt Chase painting from 1888, destined for exhibition at the Parrish Art Museum in New York, underwent an AI-assisted restoration process that revealed past interventions and lost composition details.
articles.content: William Merritt Chase's painting A Comfortable Corner, created around 1888, was restored by Modern Art Conservation prior to an upcoming exhibition at the Parrish Art Museum in New York. Artificial intelligence was employed during the restoration to help determine how past interventions had altered the surface and composition. A historical photograph revealed that the painting had been reduced in size during 1960s repairs, losing compositional details and obscuring the signature. By combining the historical black-and-white image with a contemporary color photograph, AI generated a composite that helped the team pinpoint discrepancies. Supported by a Bank of America grant, conservator Suzanne Siano noted that while AI provided a valuable, rapid research aid, ultimate conservation decisions relied on ultraviolet imaging, material knowledge, and manual examination. The restored artwork goes on display at the museum from November 14 to March 21, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: How Does an Artist Know When She’s Done? A Major Marisa Merz Retrospective Turns the Question on Its Head - ARTnews.com
articles.title: A Comprehensive Look at Marisa Merz's Creative World in Turin
articles.excerpt: Marking the centenary of Italian artist Marisa Merz's birth, a sweeping retrospective exhibition across three Turin institutions brings together over five decades of her artistic production.
articles.content: Marking the centenary of Italian artist Marisa Merz's birth, a sweeping retrospective exhibition titled "Marisa Merz: La danza delle ore (The Dance of the Hours)" has opened across three institutions in Turin. The exhibition reviews more than five decades of her work, with the Galleria d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea Torino focusing on her studio and home, the Fondazione Merz highlighting her material experiments, and the Castello di Rivoli exploring her metaphysical engagement with space. Born in Turin in 1926, Merz was the only female affiliate of the Arte Povera movement and became known for incorporating domestic labor and nontraditional media into her practice. Her work maintains a provisional quality, exemplified by her best-known installation, The Living Sculpture from 1966, and her unfired clay Testine series spanning from the 1970s to the 2010s. The exhibitions feature her aluminium installations, paraffin pools, and abstract graphite and painted physiognomies, alongside notes and Post-its left directly on her drawings. Additionally, the retrospective includes a 16 mm film diptych shot in Merz's apartment by Tacita Dean, alongside works by contemporary female artists such as Leonor Antunes, Thea Djordjadze, and Miriam Cahn.

articles.originalTitle: JSWD Wins Competition to Design Mixed-Use RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia - ArchDaily
articles.title: JSWD Wins Architectural Competition to Design RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh
articles.excerpt: German architecture practice JSWD has been selected to design the mixed-use RIYMAR Towers development in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following an international invited competition organized by Malcolm Reading Consultants.
articles.content: German practice JSWD has won an international invited competition to design RIYMAR Towers, a mixed-use development planned in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Organized by Malcolm Reading Consultants on behalf of RIYMAR Real Estate, the project is situated near King Fahd Road and Olaya Street. The proposed development combines residential, hospitality, office, retail, and leisure spaces, aligning with the objectives of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. The competition shortlisted five international practices, including Aedas, AtkinsRéalis, JSWD, Mesura, and ZHA. Further details regarding project area, heights, and timelines remain unannounced.

articles.originalTitle: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Birthday Exhibition at the Paris Mint - WWD
articles.title: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Exhibition at the Paris Mint
articles.excerpt: Grasse-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is opening a centenary exhibition featuring more than 250 works and objects at the Paris Mint.
articles.content: Frane-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is celebrating its centenary with a major exhibition at the Paris Mint. Entitled "Fragonard: 100 Years of Collections and Savoir-Faire," the event gathers more than 250 works and objects from the house's heritage collection. The exhibition remains open to the public through Jan. 17, 2027. Company chief executive officer Agnès Costa Webster noted that paintings from the family's collection in Grasse have been brought to Paris for the first time. Hosted at the 18th-century Hôtel de la Monnaie, the multisensory exhibition features paintings, perfume bottles, historic garments, silverware, and personal grooming accessories. The scenography was conceived by Nathalie Crinière, while Givaudan perfumer Daniela Andrier formulated scents based on 18th-century recipes specifically for the event. Visitors can also explore an onsite boutique and attend fragrance-making workshops by reservation.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site
articles.excerpt: Eight people were killed and 18 others injured when a three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, prompting multiple official investigations.
articles.content: A 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an adjacent excavation site on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, resulting in eight fatalities, including two children and two construction workers, and 18 injuries. Rescue operations concluded following the incident. A project geotechnical report had previously indicated that abutting structures required underpinning and warned that excavation vibration could adversely affect them. A March preconstruction survey documented visible cracking and rated the north masonry facade poorly. Approved excavation-support plans prescribed specific monitoring thresholds for movement and vibration. Available records do not establish whether the structure was underpinned or what the final monitoring readings showed before the collapse. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites associated with the project's firms. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, while Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez launched a separate inquiry. City records show the development had faced earlier stop-work orders during demolition phases before excavation began.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Unveils Creative Freedom for Designers
articles.excerpt: A new exhibition at the Molteni Museum in Giussano invites living designers to create one-of-a-kind, expressive works using existing pieces from Molteni Group brands as a starting point.
articles.content: Hosted at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, a new Molteni Museum exhibition grants living designers the creative freedom to craft one-of-a-kind works without commercial or engineering constraints. Using existing pieces from Molteni&C, UniFor, and Citterio as starting points, notable practices and designers such as Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners Industrial Design, Patricia Urquiola, and Vincent Van Duysen contributed expressive installations. Herzog & de Meuron reinterpreted a special-edition chair with playful inflatable cushions, while Ron Gilad transformed a kitchen island design into a poetic water fountain as a tribute to late designer Luca Meda. Other participants, including OMA and AMDL Circle, adopted surreal approaches through material experimentation. The exhibition will remain on display at the museum for one year before embarking on an international tour to a yet-to-be-determined roster of global cities.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Frieda Ekotto to Deliver Lecture at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale
articles.excerpt: Frieda Ekotto will deliver a lecture examining the repair practices in the works of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event takes place on November 20, 2026, at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.
articles.content: Frieda Ekotto will present a lecture examining the gathering, wrapping, repairing, and regenerating actions central to the practices of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event is scheduled for November 20, 2026, from 16:00 to 17:30 at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale. The discussion explores processes that redirect materials, labor, and time toward connections between land, body, and community that extraction seeks to disrupt. These actions form a resilience rooted in acts of refusal. By framing disobedience as the foundation of resilience, the lecture recasts the work of both artists as a sustained challenge to damaging value systems, pointing toward a relational model of authorship. Rasha Salti will introduce and moderate the session. Admission to the venue is free until capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | ZIAD ANTAR | Bladder Diplomacy - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Ziad Antar Presents Bladder Diplomacy Lecture Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for Biennale Arte 2026, Bladder Diplomacy weaves together international diplomacy, agricultural habits in the eastern Mediterranean, and personal family stories through a satirical performance.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia hosts the lecture performance Bladder Diplomacy at Tese dei Soppalchi on 18 November 2026, running from 16:00 to 17:20. The event weaves stories of international diplomacy and the cultivation of potatoes and tomatoes in the eastern Mediterranean together with personal family narratives. The work examines radical interventions in the natural environment and nutritional habits introduced to the region by modernization and globalized agribusiness. Lebanese artists Ziad Antar, Hatem Imam, and Nayla Mabsout collaborate on the performance, drawing a satirical puzzle of malicious weeds, civil wars, and the resilience of indigenous seeds. The script is written by Ziad Antar, directed by Hatem Imam, and features video by Nayla Mabsout, with Ziad Antar and Nayla Mabsout performing. Visitors must hold a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026 in order to attend the scheduled event.

articles.originalTitle: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere, Stages Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Loro Piana Honors Finest Cashmere at New York Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Italian luxury house Loro Piana presented the 2025 Cashmere of the Year Award and opened its Master of Cashmere exhibition in New York.
articles.content: Italian luxury house Loro Piana presented the 2025 Cashmere of the Year Award during a ceremony at The Brant Foundation in New York. The event highlighted a fiber fineness of 12.89 microns. Established in 2015, the award program recognizes herders who contribute to improving cashmere fineness. This 11th edition honored three couples of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia. The first prize was awarded for 135.8 kg of greasy cashmere with a fiber diameter of 12.89 microns, followed by second and third prizes for 87.1 kg at 13.01 microns and 116 kg at 13.04 microns, respectively. The gathering also featured the opening of the Master of Cashmere exhibition, showcasing the house's history and manufacturing expertise. Company executives emphasized long-standing relationships with herders originating from the 1980s and a shared commitment to quality. Discussions during the event touched upon the Loro Piana Method selective breeding program and the Resilient Threads initiative created in partnership with international organizations to support ecosystems and biodiversity in Mongolia's Sukhbaatar Province. Controlled by LVMH since 2013, the brand also manages other international initiatives, including the Record Bale Award for merino wool.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City Shared by Two Empires
articles.excerpt: A Victoria and Albert Museum guide examines the rich history and art traditions of the city that maintained its strategic position across Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman eras.
articles.content: Originally established as Nova Roma by Roman Emperor Constantine I in 330 CE, the city served as the center of the Byzantine Empire and later became the capital of the Ottoman Empire following its fall in 1453. Positioned at the meeting point of Asia and Europe, the settlement flourished through vital sea routes, attracting merchants, scholars, and pilgrims from diverse regions. According to the museum guide, monumental engineering feats such as the Theodosian Walls and the Aqueduct of Valens guaranteed the security of the metropolis across centuries. Transitioning through Roman paganism, Christianity, and majority Islamic traditions, the city's inhabitants fostered two distinct streams of art and design. The exhibition highlights this heritage through ivory plaques, manuscripts, cameos, and precious metalwork. While Byzantine Constantinople integrated sacred images into daily and political life, Ottoman culture often expressed reverence through intricate calligraphy. Historical objects, including restoration inscriptions and architectural fragments, document the enduring defensive and aesthetic ambitions of the imperial capital.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach: Highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Showcases Digital Art and Contemporary Masterpieces
articles.excerpt: Taking place at a cultural crossroads in the Americas, Art Basel Miami Beach unites voices in contemporary art while highlighting new frontiers in digital creations.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach presents a program that unites prominent voices in contemporary art alongside innovative presentations. The regional art fair brings together modern masterpieces and emerging talent on a single platform. The Zero 10 platform, dedicated to digital-era art, returns with Generation, its largest presentation to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, the exhibition spans 19 projects and explores connections between digital technologies and traditional art forms. Encompassing algorithmic art, immersive environments, painting, sculpture, and textiles, the presentation highlights works by creators such as Sarah Meyohas, Jon Rafman, and Studio Drift. Refik Anadol's collaboration with the Yawanawá community transforms Amazonian artwork, music, and weather data into evolving digital imagery. Meanwhile, Harm van den Dorpel draws on historical geometric drawings to produce generative pieces that unfold in real time during the event.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.

articles.originalTitle: Miami Beach Director and Mendes Wood DM founders on the fair's bold new changes - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Prepares Bold Layout Changes for 24th Edition
articles.excerpt: Celebrating its 24th year, Art Basel Miami Beach is revamping its floor plan and gallery configuration to create a more navigable environment and enhance experiences for exhibitors.
articles.content: Approaching its 24th year, Art Basel Miami Beach is implementing significant changes to its layout and gallery configuration. Fair Director Bridget Finn and Mendes Wood DM co-founders Matthew Wood and Pedro Mendes discussed the updates prompted by exhibitor feedback. The alterations aim to allow collectors to navigate the fair more easily and give every gallery presentation due attention. The layout shifts from five plazas to a more symmetrical configuration of four, with redesigned entrances and improved sight lines. Alongside architectural updates, the fair continues to highlight the cultural movement between North America, Latin America, and the Caribbean. The Mendes Wood DM founders noted that the event balances the spirit of discovery with necessary financial transactions. Director Bridget Finn stated that success will be measured by the success of the participating galleries and the new connections formed. Art Basel Miami Beach is scheduled to take place from December 4 to December 6, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Probably by Camille Corot | Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli | L814 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Tivoli Landscape Attributed to Camille Corot at the National Gallery
articles.excerpt: A work thought to be by French artist Camille Corot from around 1826 in Italy is held in the National Gallery collection, featuring architectural sections and light contrasts.
articles.content: French artist Camille Corot produced 200 drawings and 150 oil studies during his stay in Italy between 1825 and 1828. Due to the scarcity of signatures on these sketches, attributions remain uncertain. The work titled Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli presents a visually satisfying vista from giant doors towards light coming through upper windows. Tivoli, a town northeast of Rome, was a frequent destination for artists due to its dramatic landscape. While signed Corot on the lower right, the sketch also bears the signature Granet in a likely more recent hand. Measuring 29.7 by 21.5 centimetres, the oil on paper laid on canvas is part of the Gere Collection on long-term loan to the National Gallery and is not currently on display. Corot's dedication to close observation of nature significantly influenced the later Impressionist approach to landscape painting.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas Painting Promenade beside the Sea at The National Gallery
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's early oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, created around 1860 and depicting the Bay of Naples, is held at The National Gallery in London.
articles.content: Created around 1860 by Edgar Degas, Promenade beside the Sea stands as an early oil sketch exploring the recurrent theme of horses and riders. The artwork depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback riding along a coastal route towards cliffs. A gentleman in black with a top hat and a lady sitting side-saddle in a dark riding habit make their way past coastal vegetation. The setting has been identified as the Bay of Naples, a location Degas visited during trips to see his Italian family. Open brushwork conveys the movement of the horses' gait, while impasto captures the energy of breaking waves. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 centimeters, the oil on canvas is on long-term loan from the Gere Collection to The National Gallery in London, cataloged under inventory number L819. Evidence indicates the left-hand section derives from a notebook sketch housed in Paris. The composition reflects the artist's lifelong interest in movement and motion prior to the emergence of the Impressionist group.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.
